text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. Clinical laboratory science and hospital management are female-majority fields in most countries, so an all-woman panel of four is close to what chance would produce. Raising it makes you look aggrieved rather than analytical, and it weakens any genuine complaint you might later have.

Your stronger ground is substantive: a PhD plus eight years running a section against a master's plus a management course is a real gap, and "broad leadership experience" is vague. But hiring panels legitimately weight management capability, interview performance and fit above research credentials.

Chase the written explanation — two weeks' silence may breach your employer's policy or local law. Judge the reasoning, not the panel's sex.
